subject: Social Science
central_question: How do economic and non-economic activities differ, and how do both contribute value to individuals, families and society?
in_scope_units: Everyday work around Anu and Kabir — paid employment, family work and volunteering
Economic and non-economic activities — money, money's worth, market exchange and unpaid care
Salary and volunteering — one person may perform both economic and non-economic work
Types of payment — salary, fee, wage and payment in kind
Value addition — skill, time and effort transforming materials into more valuable goods
The importance of non-economic activities — care, gratitude, love and respect
Sevā or selfless service — community kitchens and contributing without expecting return
Community participation — Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, Van Mahotsav and festival cooperation
banned_topics: Primary, secondary and tertiary sector classification from Chapter 14
Measuring national income or gross domestic product

known_pitfalls.correction: Unpaid care, volunteering and community service create important social and personal value.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every activity performed by one person belongs to the same category.
known_pitfalls.correction: Rohan's salaried software job is economic, while his unpaid weekend teaching is non-economic.
The chapter describes salary, fee, wage and payment in kind, such as Sahil receiving mangoes of equal value.

recommended_example_progression: Identify and classify activities using the Anu and Kabir story table.
Compare Kabir's grandfather with school teachers to distinguish purpose and compensation.
Compare salary, fee, wage and payment in kind using the Kavya story.
Explain value addition using the Rajesh carpenter example.
Connect compensation, community service and value.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Refer to the chapter-end 'Questions, activities and projects' Questions 1-4 on page 193.
